content.thinking:
The 3 "failures" are test-side index errors, not implementation errors:

1. "cl leading zeros ok": `wl(req(cl="0005"), -2)` — split("\r\n") with negative index doesn't work? Actually split produces a list; `[-2]` should work... The wire: lines joined + "\r\n\r\n" + body. split("\r\n") on "....\r\nContent-Length: 5\r\n\r\nhello" → [..., "Content-Length: 5", "", "hello"]. So [-2] is "" and [-1] is "hello". The Content-Length is [-3]. My expected index wrong. Actually got "" — index -2 is the empty separator. Fix: [-3].

2. "ctype htab kept": index 6 is PAI line because there are 8 header lines: 0 method, 1 From, 2 To, 3 Call-ID, 4 CSeq, 5 Privacy, 6 PAI, 7 Content-Type, 8 Content-Length. I forgot PAI at index 6. Fix indices: ctype at 7.

3. "ctype absent": with no Content-Type: 0 method,1 From,2 To,3 Call-ID,4 CSeq,5 Privacy,6 PAI,7 Content-Length → index 7.

Fix these three test expectations.

content.text: 3 failures are test-side index errors (I forgot the PAI line shifts wire indices). Let me fix the test expectations:

arguments.command:
cd /workspace && python3 - << 'PYEOF'
src = open("tmp/tests2.py").read()
src = src.replace('wl(req(cl="0005"), -2)', 'wl(req(cl="0005"), -3)')
src = src.replace('wl(req(ctype="text/plain\\t;x=1"), 6)', 'wl(req(ctype="text/plain\\t;x=1"), 7)')
src = src.replace('wl(req(ctype=None), 6)', 'wl(req(ctype=None), 7)')
open("tmp/tests2.py","w").write(src)
PYEOF
python3 tmp/tests2.py 2>&1 | tail -3
